note: This is the first clean full week of GA4 booking tracking since the October break. sevenrooms_booking_complete fired on all seven days at all three properties, against five of seven last week. The test used is GA4 create-path bookings divided by SevenRooms website booking rows, because SevenRooms cannot be affected by anything on our own site: Aqua NYC 1.44 (239 against 166 rows), Hutong NYC 1.02 (148 against 145) and Hutong Miami 0.98 (55 against 56). The pre-break norms were 1.59 to 1.70, 1.12 to 1.15 and 1.22 to 1.29. The denominator has not settled. Recomputing last week's SevenRooms website covers a week on returned figures 5 to 9 per cent lower as cancellations accrued, so on a settled-equivalent basis these ratios are about 1.53, 1.09 and 1.04. On that reading Aqua NYC and Hutong NYC are recording normally. Hutong Miami sits below its own norm for a second week and should be checked again. Nothing on this page is scaled, substituted or filled in. The week straddles a month boundary, so the weekly target is pro-rated across both months by days in each month: October target ÷ 31 × 6 days plus November target ÷ 30 × 1 day. That gives Aqua NYC 525 (2,394 and 1,842 monthly), Hutong NYC 468 (2,100 and 1,837) and Hutong Miami 120 (530 and 509, both derived), 1,113 for the market. This basis does not reproduce the last published straddle week. At w2026-09-28 the published targets of 540, 438 and 119 were built as each month's target ÷ 30 × days, not days in month, and on that older basis this week would read 540, 481 and 123, or 1,144. The days-in-month basis is used here and the difference is recorded rather than hidden. The year-to-date target is extended from last week's published cumulative by this week's target, as in prior weeks, because it is not reproducible from the workbook by any day-count rule tested. Basis. GA4 bookings are the create path only: the modify, manage and prearrival pages, where the same event fires when a guest amends a booking, are excluded. The amendment share this week was 11.6 per cent of all booking events across the market, against 8.8 per cent in the year-ago week, so the create-path rule again costs 2026 more than it costs 2025 here. By venue it is 10.8 per cent at Aqua NYC, 11.9 per cent at Hutong NYC and 14.1 per cent at Hutong Miami, against 16.6, 0.0 and 4.3 per cent last year. Hutong New York's 2025 week still carries no modify route at all, which is why its year-on-year reads worse than the others on this basis. Current, prior, year-ago, year-to-date and the eight-week series are all on the create path, so every comparison here is like for like. They do not tie to the figures published up to and including w2026-10-05. Aqua NYC is restricted to its own venue paths in both years; the year-ago week carries no foreign rows, so the restriction changes nothing and is kept for consistency. USA targets are strategic and deliberately aggressive, Hutong NYC explicitly so: its plan hinges on website conversion rising from 4.83 to 6.5 per cent and on a large Meta efficiency fix. Hutong Miami's GA4 target is derived, not given: the workbook plans Meta bookings only, so the monthly Meta figure is scaled by 6738/4756. Google booking conversions and modelled store visits settle upward for two to three weeks and have done so again, which is why the prior week is re-pulled every run and never carried: Hutong NYC's W42 booking conversions moved from 16.0 as published to 26.0, and its walk-in signals from 318 to 477. Ad spend rose sharply and the bookings did not follow in one place. Aqua NYC's Meta spend went from $1,810 to $2,869, and $1,158 of that sits in a single Halloween landing-page-view campaign that recorded no booking conversions at all, which is also why the account's clicks went from 5,321 to 17,409. Hutong NYC's Google spend nearly doubled from $1,166 to $2,150, and $998 of it went to a new Search > Midtown campaign returning 3 booking conversions, a cost per booking of about $333, while its Search > Brand campaign returned 16 for $290.
